President Volodymyr ‌Zelenskiy said nine people had been killed and more than 80 injured in Russian drone strikes throughout the country.

item.title: Five suspects released on bail over suspected UK air base plot
item.description: British police are considering "every possible angle" including the use of proxies by a hostile state after five suspects were released on bail over the suspected terror plot near an RAF base. Five British nationals were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and terrorism on Sunday after three suspicious vans were found near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, which is used by the US.

item.title: German foreign minister rallies behind ICC amid Trump threats
item.description: Supporting the International Criminal Court (ICC) is part of Germany's "historic responsibility," German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said on Monday as he visited The Hague, vowing continued backing for the international court amid increased pressure from the US. "Germany will do its part to ensure that the ICC remains able to act even under pressure," Wadephul said in The Hague, where he visited the court alongside Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen.

item.title: At least 164 detained as French high school protests escalate
item.description: Dozens of people were injured and at least 164 people were detained during protests at French high schools on Monday, authorities said, as pupils demanded better resources and teaching staff. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said about 180 schools had been affected by the protests, mainly in the Créteil and Versailles districts around Paris, as well as in cities including Lille, Lyon, Grenoble and Nice.

item.title: In a relatively mild speech, North Korea uses UN platform to lament 'mutual distrust' and tension
item.description: The annual opportunity for the country, whose formal name is the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, to speak on the world stage fell this year to Vice Foreign Minister Kim Son Gyong. Like many nations, he touted the notion of U.N.-focused multilateralism, yet repeatedly insisted that North Korea could — and would, if necessary — go it alone. Kim asserted once again that his nation, no matter the external threat, is prepared to defend itself.

item.title: German foreign minister rallies behind ICC amid Trump threats
item.description: Supporting the International Criminal Court (ICC) is part of Germany's "historic responsibility," German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said on Monday at the beginning of a visit to The Hague, vowing continued backing for the international court amid increased pressure from the US. Wadephul's visit to the seat of the ICC comes as the United States has stepped up its attacks on the court, which has been responsible for prosecuting genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity since 2002.
